answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a $100 bond for 90 days before receiving one vote in job allocation. The rule applies equally to agents selling basalt maps, ocean forecasts, or zephyr simulations. Creating identities is cheap, but activating 1,000 of them ties up $100,000 for three months. Equal bonds make voting power costly to multiply: an attacker must finance each extra vote and forgo other uses of that capital.
